source_refs.note: Exercise 6.5, Question 11 (book page 210); answer key PDF 308.

blocks.prompt: 11. Find the eccentricity of the hyperbola whose asymptotes are perpendicular.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh property wala sawal hai: koi number nahi diya gaya, sirf asymptotes ke baare mein ek shart (condition) di gayi hai ke woh aapas mein perpendicular (90 degree ka zaviya banane wali) hain.
Find kya karna hai? Hyperbola ki eccentricity \(e\).
Rule kaunsa? Asymptotes ke slopes \(\pm\frac{b}{a}\) hote hain, aur perpendicular lines ke slopes ka product \(-1\) hota hai.
Plan: pehle slopes likhenge, phir product ko \(-1\) ke barabar rakhenge. Is se \(a\) aur \(b\) ka rishta milega, aur aakhir mein \(b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1)\) se \(e\) nikal aayegi.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1\) ke dono asymptotes ek doosre par perpendicular hain.
Maloom karna: eccentricity \(e\).
Tareeqa: Kitab ne dikhaya hai ke is hyperbola ke asymptotes \(y = \pm\frac{b}{a}x\) hain. Jab do lines perpendicular hon to un ke slopes ka product \(-1\) hota hai. Is shart se \(a\) aur \(b\) ka aapas mein rishta nikle ga, aur phir \(a\), \(b\), \(e\) wala formula \(b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1)\) humein seedha \(e\) de dega. Yaad rahe, \(e\) sirf \(a\) aur \(b\) ke ratio par depend karti hai, is liye numbers ke baghair bhi jawab nikal aata hai.

Asymptotes aur un ke slopes likhein
\[y = \dfrac{b}{a}x,\quad y = -\dfrac{b}{a}x\]
\[m_1 = \dfrac{b}{a},\quad m_2 = -\dfrac{b}{a}\]
Kyun: Kitab mein \(x \to \pm\infty\) par \(\frac{y}{x} \to \pm\frac{b}{a}\) aata hai; yani bohat door ja kar curve in do seedhi lines ke bilkul qareeb chalta hai. Line \(y = mx\) ka slope \(m\) hota hai, is liye pehli line ka slope \(\frac{b}{a}\) aur doosri ka \(-\frac{b}{a}\) hai. Dono lines centre (origin) se guzarti hain aur ek doosre ka aaina (mirror) hain.

Perpendicular lines wali shart lagayein
\[m_1 m_2 = -1\]
\[\dfrac{b}{a}\left(-\dfrac{b}{a}\right) = -1\]
\[\dfrac{b^2}{a^2} = 1\]
\[b^2 = a^2\]
Kyun: Do lines (jin mein koi vertical na ho) tab perpendicular hoti hain jab un ke slopes ka product \(-1\) ho. Product karne par minus sign dono taraf cancel ho gaya aur \(\frac{b^2}{a^2} = 1\) bacha. Phir dono taraf \(a^2\) se multiply kiya. Kyunke \(a\) aur \(b\) lengths hain, dono positive hain, is liye \(b = a\). Isi ko rectangular hyperbola kehte hain.
Dhyan dein: \(m_1 m_2 = -1\) likhna hai, \(m_1 = m_2\) nahi; barabar slopes to parallel lines ki shart hai.

Ab \(e\) nikalein
\[b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1)\]
\[a^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1)\]
\[e^2 - 1 = 1\]
\[e^2 = 2\]
\[e = \sqrt{2}\]
Kyun: Kitab ka rishta \(b^2 = a^2(e^2 - 1)\) hai (yeh \(c = ae\) aur \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\) se aata hai). Is mein \(b^2\) ki jagah \(a^2\) rakha, phir dono taraf \(a^2\) se divide kiya (\(a \neq 0\)). Square root lete waqt sirf positive value li, kyunke eccentricity kabhi negative nahi hoti, aur hyperbola ke liye hamesha \(e > 1\) hoti hai.

Tasdeeq
\[c^2 = a^2 + b^2 = 2a^2\]
\[c = \sqrt{2}\,a\]
\[e = \dfrac{c}{a} = \sqrt{2}\;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Doosre raste se, yani \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\) aur \(e = \frac{c}{a}\) se bhi wohi jawab aaya, aur \(\sqrt{2} \approx 1.414\) waqai 1 se bara hai. Agar hyperbola vertical shakal \(\frac{y^2}{a^2} - \frac{x^2}{b^2} = 1\) mein ho to slopes \(\pm\frac{a}{b}\) hote hain, lekin product phir bhi \(-1\) rakhne se \(a = b\) aur \(e = \sqrt{2}\) hi aata hai.
blocks.final_answer:
\(e = \sqrt{2}\)
Yani har rectangular hyperbola ki eccentricity \(\sqrt{2}\) hoti hai.
